mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of periods with declining GDP, or GDP growth and SPX returns show no significant negative correlation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% in a single month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5%, it signals a weakening demand environment coupled with labor market stress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases > 10% in 1 month and UNRATE > 5%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of HOUST decline and high UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) for three consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed may tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 50% of periods with sustained CPI increase, or CPI growth and SPX returns show no significant negative correlation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by less than 100,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is rising, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment turns negative.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases < 100,000 in 1 month and UNRATE is rising
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of weak PAYEMS growth and rising UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% in a single month signals a weakening consumer demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending is a key driver of economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS decline and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
